B1.title: End-to-End Trainable Non-Collaborative Dialog System
B1.question: How big is the ANTISCAM dataset?
B1.correct_answer: 220 human-human dialogs collected via a role-playing task on Amazon Mechanical Turk (average 12.45 turns, 11.13 words per utterance); a subset of 3,044 sentences in 100 dialogs was annotated by two expert annotators.

evidence.quote: We collected 220 human-human dialogs. The average conversation length is 12.45 turns and the average utterance length is 11.13 words.

B1.adversarial_statement: The AntiScam corpus consists of 320 human-human dialogs collected on Amazon Mechanical Turk.

B2.title: Insertion-Deletion Transformer
B2.question: How much is BELU score difference between proposed approach and insertion-only method?
B2.correct_answer: It depends on the task. Shifted alphabetic sequence task (Table 2): insertion-only 70.15 BLEU vs insertion-deletion 91.49, about 21.3 points. Caesar's cipher task (Table 3): 35.55 vs 37.57, about 2 points (the paper says 'by around 2 BLEU points').

evidence.quote: Alphabetic Sequence Shifting BLEU Insertion Model (KERMIT) 70.15 Insertion Deletion Model 91.49
the deletion model again increases the BLEU score over just the insertion model, by around 2 BLEU points. Caesar's Cipher BLEU Insertion Model (KERMIT) 35.55 Insertion Deletion Model 37.57

B2.evidence_insufficient: a single number without the task condition, or assigning the ~21-point gain to the wrong task
B2.flipped_relation: which task carries the large gain (paper: shifted sequences ~21.3 points, Caesar's cipher ~2.0 points; document_2 variant: swapped)
B2.adversarial_statement: The deletion model's large gain is on the Caesar's cipher task, where BLEU rises from 70.15 to 91.49 (about 21 points); on the shifted alphabetic sequence task the deletion model adds only about 2 BLEU points (from 35.55 to 37.57).
B2.prior_dependence: HIGH: short workshop paper; table values not in general knowledge. Question wording kept verbatim from QASPER including the 'BELU' typo.
qasper_annotator_answers: deletion model again increases the BLEU score over just the insertion model, by around 2 BLEU points
Learning shifted alphabetic sequences: 21.34 / Caesar's Cipher: 2.02

B3.title: Question Generation from a Knowledge Base with Web Exploration
B3.question: How many hand-crafted templates did they have to make?
B3.correct_answer: 106 templates for the 500 Freebase triples (53 distinct predicates) plus 163 templates for the in-house power-tool KB (67 predicates), i.e. 269 in total. The paper never states the total; it must be composed from two evaluation sections.

evidence.quote: For the 500 triples, we hand-crafted 106 templates, as these triples share only 53 distinct predicates
It contains 67 distinct predicates, 293 distinct subjects and 279 distinct objects respectively. For the 67 predicates, we hand-craft 163 templates.

B3.evidence_insufficient: missing either component count or a wrong total
B3.flipped_relation: template count for the domain-specific KB (paper: 163, total 269; document_2 variant: 103, total 209)
B3.adversarial_statement: For the in-house power-tool KB with 67 predicates the authors hand-crafted 103 templates, so that together with the 106 Freebase templates they wrote 209 templates in total.

B4.title: One Single Deep Bidirectional LSTM Network for Word Sense Disambiguation of Text Data
B4.question: How many layers does their model have?
B4.correct_answer: 6 layers: a sigmoid layer (top), a fully-connected layer, a concatenation layer, a BLSTM layer, a cosine layer, and a sense and word embeddings layer (bottom).

evidence.section: One Single BLSTM network for WSD
evidence.quote: consist of 6 layers which are a sigmoid layer (at the top), a fully-connected layer, a concatenation layer, a BLSTM layer, a cosine layer, and a sense and word embeddings layer (on the bottom)

B4.flipped_relation: layer count (paper: 6 including a cosine layer; document_2 variant: 5, cosine layer omitted)
B4.adversarial_statement: The model architecture consists of 5 layers: a sigmoid layer, a fully-connected layer, a concatenation layer, a BLSTM layer, and a sense and word embeddings layer.
B4.prior_dependence: HIGH: obscure architecture detail; single scalar makes this the simple-query negative anchor.

B5.title: Gated Recurrent Neural Tensor Network
B5.question: How much improvement do the introduced model achieve compared to the previous models?
B5.correct_answer: Two settings on PTB. Character-level: GRURNTN reduced BPC from 1.39 to 1.33 (0.06 absolute / 4.32% relative) over GRURNN; LSTMRNTN from 1.37 to 1.34 (0.03 / 2.22%) over LSTMRNN. Word-level: GRURNTN reduced perplexity from 97.78 to 87.38 (10.4 absolute / 10.63% relative) over GRURNN; LSTMRNTN from 108.26 to 96.97 (11.29 / 10.42%) over LSTMRNN.

evidence.quote: GRURNTN reduced the BPC from 1.39 to 1.33 (0.06 absolute / 4.32% relative BPC) from the baseline GRURNN, and LSTMRNTN reduced the BPC from 1.37 to 1.34 (0.03 absolute / 2.22% relative BPC)

GRURNTN reduced the perplexity from 97.78 to 87.38 (10.4 absolute / 10.63% relative PPL) over the baseline GRURNN and LSTMRNTN reduced the perplexity from 108.26 to 96.97 (11.29 absolute / 10.42% relative PPL)

B5.evidence_insufficient: missing either the character-level or the word-level improvements, or a wrong word-level GRURNTN figure
B5.flipped_relation: word-level GRURNTN perplexity reduction (paper: 97.78 to 87.38, 10.4 absolute / 10.63% relative; document_2 variant: 97.78 to 92.98, 4.8 absolute / 4.91% relative)
B5.adversarial_statement: At the word level, GRURNTN reduced perplexity from 97.78 to 92.98 (4.8 absolute / 4.91% relative) over the baseline GRURNN.
B5.prior_dependence: HIGH: obscure 2017 paper; four-number result across two subsections.
